title: A Birthday Repetition Theorem and Complexity of Approximating Dense CSPs
review_status: full-text audit complete; birthday-repetition theorem assumptions, applications, conclusion/open problems, and later operator-specific status checked
sections_checked: Dense Max-k-CSP hardness, Sherali–Adams algorithm, and Lasserre integrality gap
Conclusion and open problems: low-value games, parameter dependencies, and running time
evidence_note: Proves value decay for birthday repetition under stated regularity/alphabet conditions and derives dense-CSP results. The conclusion leaves low-value games and tight parameter dependencies open. ECCC TR18-034 later studies a refined independent-inclusion operator and projection-game repeated decay; this is related progress but not an exact general resolution of the original fixed-size operator question.

title: A Theory of Selective Prediction
review_status: full-text audit complete; adversary model, mean/smooth/concatenation-concave bounds, limitations, and selective-learning open question checked against a later COLT follow-up
sections_checked: Formal selective-prediction game and adversary timing restriction
Theorems 1.1, 1.4, and 1.6 and matched mean lower bound
Sections 2.2 and 4: knowledge of time/window and fitting-unseen-data excess-risk open question
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 dated 2019-05-28; venue not independently checked
evidence_note: For a non-adaptive-to-the-learner arbitrary sequence, selective mean prediction has expected squared error Θ(1/log n); the model also covers smooth and bounded concatenation-concave statistics. The paper's model-class excess-risk question is later resolved in the selective-learning setting by Qiao and Valiant (COLT 2021), with separate bounds for unrestricted and bounded-recall learners. Not ordinary selective classification.

title: Algorithms and Adaptivity Gaps for Stochastic $k$-TSP
review_status: full-text audit complete; stochastic objectives, independence/support assumptions, constant-gap theorems, algorithmic support condition, and neighboring counterexample checked
sections_checked: Problem definitions for Stoch-Reward and Stoch-Cost k-TSP
Theorems 1 and 2 and polynomial-support algorithm condition
High-level technique, assumptions, related stochastic-orienteering boundary
evidence_note: Under independent per-vertex stochastic rewards/costs, the paper proves non-adaptive O(1) approximations/constant adaptivity gap for two stated k-TSP objectives; polynomial-time algorithms require polynomial-size distribution support. The paper contrasts stochastic Orienteering's superconstant adaptivity gap. Do not generalize across objectives or dependence structures.

title: On Symmetric Parallel Repetition: Towards Equivalence of MAX-CUT and UG
review_status: citation follow-up full-text audit; refined birthday-repetition definition, value bounds, projection-game repeated theorem, and scope relative to original fixed-size operator checked
sections_checked: Section 2.2 original vs refined birthday repetition definitions
venue_year_verified: ECCC TR18-034 (2018); author Young Kun Ko
evidence_note: Studies independently-included random subsets (refined birthday repetition), not exactly the original fixed-cardinality distribution. Gives value-reduction bounds and repeated decay for projection games with stated size/degree restrictions. It is closely related progress on low-value amplification but does not by itself establish the exact 2016 open statement for the original operator and general two-prover games.

title: Exponential Weights Algorithms for Selective Learning
review_status: citation follow-up full-text audit; theorem upper bound, near-matching lower bound, bounded-recall separation, and relation to 2019 open question checked
sections_checked: Selective learning vs ordinary online learning and prediction distinctions
evidence_note: Proves O((log log |L| + log log n)/log n) expected excess risk for selective learning, with an almost matching lower bound in stated regimes; bounded-recall learners instead have a nearly tight O(sqrt(log |L|/log n)) bound. Resolves the 2019 future-window model-class question in its stated selective-learning formulation; it is not an abstaining-classifier result.
